executive_assessment.text: Karakalpakstan's named target districts and Baday-Tugay communities add water, livelihood, finance and participation detail; summary-based findings lack district-resolved measurements.

Historical UNDP warning/advisory reach and 2026 restoration consultations document capacities and process, not independently measured resilience effects. Regional water-tension scenarios are not domestic conflict forecasts.

geographic_notes.text: GGGI's March 2025 publisher summary identifies restricted water supply in Bozataw, Chimbay, Karauzyak and Kegeyli, associated with upstream diversion and climate change; their separate contributions are not measured.
GGGI's March 2025 summary reports poverty-related adaptation constraints, particularly among young women and dehkan farmers in its four-district target area.
GGGI's March 2025 summary describes expensive formal finance, limited formal management training and missing climate strategies among target-area farmer groups.

At project closeout, UNDP reported 10 automated meteorological stations and two equipped hydrological posts in Karakalpakstan, supporting drought early warnings with six-to-eight months' lead time for the lower Amu Darya.
Three project advisory centers in Nukus and Kegeyli district served 21,200 farmers and household-land owners, including more than 6,000 women, according to UNDP's 2021 closeout account.
UNDP reports that 41,200 people applied resource-saving climate-resilient agriculture and 43,750 farmers used water-saving practices such as laser leveling and drip irrigation in Karakalpakstan.

Participants near the Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve and Baday-Tugay connected land degradation with insufficient irrigation and drinking water, limited employment, and high agricultural costs; they identified reliable water as essential for restoration.

Under FOLUR-Uzbekistan, farmers, pastoralists, women, protected-area staff, communities, and authorities reviewed restoration proposals, identified priority sites, and discussed implementation and maintenance roles across three regions, including Karakalpakstan.

Karakalpakstan participants supported restoring degraded Tugay forests near Baday-Tugay with native riparian species; FAO reports that water access and livelihood pressures will affect sustained community participation.

known_gaps.text: The 2021 NDC records government projections and planned adaptation; implementation status and updated subnational risk data were not checked.
The World Bank CCDR release does not provide the underlying model assumptions for the 2030 population-risk or 2050 economy estimates.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
No country-specific primary evidence was found that climate change caused violent conflict in Uzbekistan; NUPI's source-stated tension pathway is conditional and regional.

No evidence was located linking FCV events to blocked adaptation access, interruption of a named project, or reduced resilience delivery; the June 2022 protest trigger was constitutional, not climate-related.

Detailed methods and district-level figures for GGGI's four-district risk profile remain unavailable because the full report PDF could not be read; the Atlas was excluded because it is marked for internal use only.

The 2021 UNDP project counts are closeout-reported reach and practices, not independently measured climate-resilience impacts; the FAO 2026 account describes consultations and proposed restoration rather than completed outcomes.
The public-hosted Atlas marked internal-use-only was excluded; its substantive extracted claims were removed from the uncommitted intake before publication.
GGGI's target-area poverty/training percentages are not adopted as population estimates without methods, thresholds or sample vintage.
No new complete local climate-violence or reverse-FCV chain is inferred; the transboundary tension warning remains regional and conditional.
